subject: Payment holdback on Azure private listing SOW - need decision
messages:
From: Evelyn Zhang <evelyn.zhang@astramed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment routing for Azure private listing (SOW attached)

Hi Irene / team,

Thanks again for the call today. Internal procurement asked us to confirm one thing before we sign: AstraMed legal is proposing a 10% payment holdback tied to delivery acceptance milestones for the first 90 days (mkt pilot). They want the PO to reflect a single final invoice but with 10% retained and released after acceptance sign-off (they can provide the acceptance checklist).

This is a bit different from the standard Azure private listing invoicing flow we discussed — can Redwood accept a single invoice with a contractual holdback and still have the marketplace route the invoice to Microsoft (so they pay and remit)? Alternatively, AstraMed can split the invoice but would prefer single invoice/holdback if Marketplace supports it.

I've attached the SOW with AstraMed's requested payment language highlighted. Please let me know if this is something your finance/legal can agree to or if Azure Marketplace routing will block this pattern.

Evelyn
Procurement Lead | AstraMed
(attachment: SOW_AstraMed_v3.pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Zhang <evelyn.zhang@astramed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment routing for Azure private listing (SOW attached)

Evelyn — thanks for surfacing this. We discussed with Finance briefly and this raises two separate workstreams: 1) Redwood's willingness to accept a contractual holdback, and 2) whether Azure Marketplace invoicing/routing can accommodate the retained amount and release flow.

Quick answers:
- From a Redwood contractual perspective, we can consider a holdback but need Legal sign-off on the exact clause and the acceptance criteria. Looping in Rishi for legal on redlines.
- Marketplace routing is trickier. My understanding is that Microsoft typically expects seller invoices for the gross amount and then handles settlement via the Merchant Partner model. They may not support a downstream automated holdback release from Microsoft to the seller — which would mean AstraMed's model would either need: (A) Marketplace to accept a split invoice (80% now, 10% holdback remitted later, 10% ???) or (B) AstraMed pays net to Microsoft and Microsoft pays Redwood the gross less their fees, leaving the holdback mechanics to AstraMed and Redwood. We will confirm with the Azure PM.

Rishi — can you review the redlined paragraph in SOW_AstraMed_v3.pdf and advise whether Redwood can accept a 10% retention with a defined acceptance checklist and 90-day release? Also flag any compliance/indemnity concerns.

Marissa / Ben — please pull the internal billing playbook for Azure private listings and confirm whether we've done a similar holdback before and how we reconciled via Marketplace.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of GTM Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment routing for Azure private listing (SOW attached)

I've reviewed the SOW redlines (see inline comments in Redlines_Azure_PO.docx). Key points: 
- Contractually we can accept a retention clause if the acceptance criteria are objective and timeboxed. Recommend replacing subjective language ("satisfactory") with a short checklist (deliverables + test criteria).
- Limit the retainage to 10% as proposed but include a cap that prevents indefinite withholding — e.g., automatic release after 120 days unless AstraMed provides dispute notice with specifics.
- Add an invoice schedule that supports either (i) split invoices (initial 90% invoice + retention invoice) or (ii) a single invoice where settlement is handled off-marketplace (if Azure can't support staged remittance). We should prefer split invoices for operational clarity.

Operationally Ben/Finance: if we proceed with split invoices, we need to confirm: (a) whether Marketplace will accept two invoices tied to the same PO; (b) how VAT/GST will be handled in split settlement; (c) whether Microsoft will withhold any additional commissions on the retained tranche. If Marketplace cannot support split invoices, Redwood can accept a single invoice but will require AstraMed to execute a side-letter that defines the holdback and release timeline (so Redwood has contract remedy).

I've attached the redlines. If Azure PM confirms technical constraints, we should propose the split-invoice compromise and an acceptance checklist.

-Rishi
Deputy GC | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redlines_Azure_PO.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Zhang <evelyn.zhang@astramed.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azure Marketplace PM <mpm@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment routing for Azure private listing (SOW attached)

Hi Evelyn — thanks for patience while we dug in. Quick operational update after a sync with the Azure Marketplace PM: Microsoft will accept split invoices tied to the same PO for private plan transactions, but they do not natively escrow or automate a retention-release workflow on behalf of buyers and sellers. Practically that means: 

Option A (recommended): AstraMed issues two invoices via Marketplace: Invoice #1 for 90% on acceptance, Invoice #2 for 10% (retention) after the acceptance checklist is signed. Microsoft will route both invoices to Redwood when they settle; Redwood will receive the 90% sooner and the 10% when AstraMed invoices it. Azure does not withhold or remit any extra commission on the retained tranche beyond normal marketplace fees (PM confirmed).

Option B: AstraMed issues a single gross invoice; AstraMed and Redwood execute a side-letter that documents the holdback. Microsoft processes the gross invoice and pays Redwood the gross less fees — Redwood then must rely on contractual mechanisms with AstraMed to collect the retention portion. This adds collection risk.

From Redwood's side, Legal (Rishi) recommends Option A — split invoices — and Finance (Ben) confirms our systems can map two invoices to a single PO as long as the PO number and SOW reference are consistent. Ben, please confirm any tax/VAT notes; Marissa will coordinate invoice routing docs with Azure.

Evelyn — if AstraMed is OK with Option A, we can update the SOW to include the acceptance checklist and invoice schedule and circulate for signature. I can also open a DocuSign envelope and attach both SOW and PO side-letter.

Next steps for AstraMed: confirm Option A or B, and if Option A, provide the acceptance checklist doc so Rishi can finalize language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
(attachment: None)
